items.t: Meadow lets you leave your smartphone at home without sacrificing the essentials
items.d: “We’re not Luddites... it’s just we don’t want social media, browsing and that kind of stuff," said 25-year-old founder Shreyas Narlanka.
items.fullText: I held my breath as I walked into the concert venue and showed the bouncer a ticket barcode on a three-inch, square screen. “If it doesn’t go through, I can try something else,” I said quickly, worried that the barcode wouldn’t work. But just as Meadow founder Shreyas Narlanka promised me, the code I scanned onto the startup’s minimalist phone earlier that day worked fine. “Cool phone,” the bouncer said, ushering me inside. I’d done it. With Meadow’s barebones smartphone, I had called an Uber, streamed Apple Music during the ride, and entered the show. Not once did I need to touch my iPhone, which I only brought with me as a backup in case the ticket scan didn’t work. “With so many dumb phones, the Brick , and everything, the messaging is like, ‘Slow down, focus on your work’ or whatever,” Narlanka says, explaining why his company chose to build a minimal phone. “But the reason we’re different is because we’re all about getting outside and unplugging and having a sick social life.” Go online, and you’ll see a growing mass of content and comments from people across the world feeling suffocated by being constantly connected via their smartphones and social media feeds. That’s resulting in a new device category that promises a reprieve. Some of these devices, like the Light Phone , require users to completely give up their smartphone and switch to a simpler device. Others, like the Wisephone , offer a modern touchscreen device with a minimal UI and a few apps. Still others are embracing more tactile form factors, like the Commodore Callback , which is a flip-phone with a touchscreen. Meadow, meanwhile, is taking the middle road, intending to simply supplement your existing device. It runs Android, and so supports apps like Maps, Strava, Uber, Apple Music and Spotify. items.t: Bill Gates says AI companies self-regulating isn’t enough and governments should be involved
items.d: Bill Gates called for lawmakers in Washington to regulate the development of artificial intelligence, weeks after the CEOs of some of the nation’s biggest AI labs agreed on the need to slow the pace of AI progress.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Bill Gates says AI companies self-regulating isn’t enough and governments should be involved in monitoring The Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist said AI is capable of helping bad actors harm billions of people. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Add to Google Bill Gates says AI 'powerful enough' to cause 'a billion deaths' 01:18 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 25, 2026, 7:00 AM EDT By Alexandra Marquez Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates on Wednesday called for lawmakers in Washington to regulate the development of artificial intelligence, weeks after the CEOs of some of the nation’s biggest AI labs agreed on the need to slow the pace of AI progress. “No one thinks self-regulation is enough,” Gates told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” in an interview set to air in full Sunday. Asked by moderator Kristen Welker whether there needs to be legislation passed in Washington, Gates said, “Absolutely.” “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” he said. “And that has to be a required thing. And it will be a little bit of overhead for the industry, but not a dramatic slowing of what they’re doing.” Earlier this month, the CEOs of Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the nation’s biggest AI labs, agreed that the race to develop powerful AI systems should slow down . Their statements on the issue came after a whistleblower who recently resigned from Anthropic, Jacob Coxon, publicly declared that “neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon added in a series of social media posts and interviews that week. items.fullText: 이코노미 > 경제 AI 투자축 GPU서 CPU·메모리로 확장…판 뒤집힌다 “삼전닉스 가치 재평가” 발행일 : 2026-09-25 19:15 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 삼성전자(왼쪽)와 SK하이닉스. 사진=연합뉴스 KB증권, AI 에이전트 확산으로 메모리 수요 확대 전망 인공지능(AI) 인프라 투자의 중심축이 그래픽처리장치(GPU)에서 중앙처리장치(CPU)와 메모리 반도체로 빠르게 이동하면서 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 전략적 가치가 재평가될 수 있다는 분석이 나왔다. AI 에이전트 확산으로 추론 연산이 늘어나면서 고대역폭메모리(HBM)는 물론 DDR5와 기업용 솔리드스테이트드라이브(eSSD)까지 AI 데이터센터 전반의 메모리 수요가 확대될 수 있다는 전망이다. 김동원 KB증권 리서치본부장은 지난 24일 최근 뉴욕 증시에서 인텔, AMD, ARM 등의 주가가 급등한 배경으로 AI 인프라 투자 범위가 GPU를 넘어 CPU와 메모리로 확대될 것이라는 기대를 꼽았다. AI 에이전트 서비스 확산으로 AI 수익화 가능성이 높아질수록 하이퍼스케일러의 인프라 투자도 장기화하고 메모리 수요에 대한 가시성 역시 높아질 수 있다는 설명이다. 특히 AI 에이전트는 기존 생성형 AI보다 빈번하고 지속적인 추론 연산을 요구한다는 점에서 메모리 산업에 새로운 수요를 만들 수 있다. AI 모델이 단순히 답변을 생성하는 것을 넘어 여러 단계의 작업을 연속적으로 수행할수록 CPU와 GPU뿐 아니라 HBM, DDR5, eSSD 등 데이터센터 전반의 메모리 사용량이 늘어날 수 있기 때문이다. 김 본부장은 AMD가 미국 반도체 업체 가운데 엔비디아, 브로드컴, 마이크론에 이어 네 번째로 시가총액 1조달러를 넘어선 점도 AI 인프라의 병목이 GPU에서 다른 부품으로 이동하고 있음을 보여주는 신호로 해석했다. 서버용 CPU 출하량이 늘어나면 고용량 DDR5 서버 D램 수요가 확대되고, GPU와 AI 가속기의 증가는 HBM 수요를 동시에 끌어올릴 수 있다는 분석이다. AI 인프라의 성능 경쟁이 연산 능력뿐 아니라 데이터를 얼마나 빠르게 공급할 수 있는지로 이동하면서 메모리의 중요성도 커지고 있다. 김 본부장은 초당 1000토큰 수준의 높은 처리 성능이 요구되는 에이전틱 AI 환경에서는 데이터 공급 속도가 핵심 경쟁력이 될 것으로 봤다. 삼성전자는 이 같은 변화에 대응해 GPU 상단에 메모리를 적층하는 차세대 HBM 기술인 'zHBM' 개발을 추진하고 있으며, 2027년 말 샘플 공급이 예상된다고 김 본부장은 설명했다. 메모리를 단순한 저장장치가 아니라 AI 연산 성능과 효율을 결정하는 핵심 인프라로 보는 시각이 확대되고 있다는 의미다. 김 본부장은 AI 데이터센터를 비유해 GPU가 심장, CPU가 두뇌, 전력이 산소라면 메모리는 데이터를 끊임없이 순환시키는 혈관이라고 설명했다. AI 모델의 규모와 추론 작업이 늘어날수록 데이터 이동량도 증가하는 만큼 메모리의 성능과 효율이 전체 시스템 경쟁력을 좌우할 가능성이 커지고 있다는 것이다. 이 같은 변화가 현실화할 경우 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스는 단순한 메모리 공급업체를 넘어 AI 인프라의 핵심 부품을 제공하는 기업으로 평가받을 가능성이 있다. GPU 중심으로 형성됐던 AI 반도체 투자 사이클이 CPU와 메모리, 저장장치 등으로 확산하면서 국내 메모리 업체들의 실적과 기업가치에 새로운 변수가 될 수 있다는 분석이다. 이상목 기자 mrlsm@etnews.com

items.t: Meta’s Muse Charm looks like a Tamagotchi, but it’s tapping into a much newer trend
items.d: Meta’s new AI gadget may look like a Tamagotchi, but its dangling form factor taps into a much broader Gen Z trend around bag charms, retro tech, and turning gadgets into fashion accessories.
items.fullText: Is Meta’s just-announced Muse Charm a playful device that will make AI more approachable to everyday consumers, or will it be yet another flop in a long list of AI hardware gadgets that didn’t take off, like the Ai Pin, Rabbit, or Friend pendant? Reactions, so far, have been mixed. What the Charm is, however, is on-trend. Like it or not, the form factor could potentially appeal to Gen Z consumers who, in this post- Labubu era, have already been into various dangling items from keychains and bags. It’s all part of a broader kitschy, retro-inspired shift in their approach to fashion and technology. Already, Gen Z has created a market for things that dangle, with everything from lip glosses to hand sanitizers to sunblocks to fragrances and more turned into bag charms , primarily targeted at women. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kristina Rodulfo (@kristinarodulfo) Hailey Bieber’s viral Rhode lip case, which stuck the lip gloss onto a phone case , had a big influence on this idea that beauty products could also be fashion accessories, as did its other beauty-focused bag charms . (The brand saw $212 million in annual net sales from a lineup of roughly 10 products, Vogue noted last year, as the company announced its billion-dollar exit to Elf Beauty.) Then there was the Labubu craze , which saw sales of the so-ugly-it’s-cute fuzzy monster bag charm explode, growing Pop Mart’s (the Chinese retailer behind the product) revenue to $1.8 billion in 2024 , a 7x jump from 2019. While demand for the Labubu itself has since faded, the concept of the decorative bag charm has not. One analyst firm estimates the global bag charm market will grow to over $1 billion by 2030 . Image Credits: LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / Contributor / Getty Images Today, bag charms can be characters, bedazzled beauty products, or other whimsical designs or objects, like Coach’s coveted cherry charms , a Gen Z favorite . items.t: Google Photos ‘Clueless’-inspired virtual closet is now available on Android and iOS
items.d: The AI-powered feature builds a virtual wardrobe from your photos, and is now broadly available after first rolling out to Android users in June.
items.fullText: Google’s new AI-powered feature that turns photos of your outfits into a virtual closet — one seemingly inspired by Cher’s iconic virtual wardrobe app featured in the movie “Clueless” — is now available to everyone in the U.S., Brazil, and India, on both iOS and Android devices. The company announced the feature earlier this year with plans to begin the rollout in the summer. Android users gained access first, starting in June, and now the virtual closet is available to all Android and iOS users in the supported markets. Image Credits: Google The idea of a digital closet in “Clueless” was meant to highlight Cher’s privileged life, where she had so many outfits that she needed a digital system to help her choose what to wear and keep everything organized. Now, you don’t have to be a rich Beverly Hills teenager to take advantage of such technology. Instead, Google uses AI technology to create a copy of your wardrobe, based on the items you wore in your photos. From the app, you can also filter items by category — like tops, bottoms, jewelry, and more — then mix and match them to create different outfits. Google says the feature is designed to assist the user, and the data about how you dress or what you wear is not being shared with third parties, like retailers. Image Credits: Google The broader rollout of the virtual closet feature arrives alongside a handful of other Google Photos updates, including a way to select, brighten, and share photos using a single prompt in Gemini Spark, an upgraded markup tool, and more Remix templates that use AI to transform your photos. (The Gemini Spark feature requires a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription in the U.S.) With Markup, you’ll be able to use a redacting pen to blur sensitive information like license plates, access precise thickness sliders for custom sketches, and pick from different fonts when adding text to photos. items.t: ElevenLabs’ CEO on margins, IPO timing, and telling customers they’re talking to a bot
items.d: ElevenLabs powers the AI voice on the other end of a lot of customer service calls, and its CEO told me this week that businesses should probably tell you that — at least until getting a machine is what everyone expects anyway.
items.fullText: ElevenLabs builds the voice layer of AI, the models that turn text into speech that sounds human. Most people encounter it when they’re talking with customer service — often without realizing it. Klarna runs first-line phone support for 35 million U.S. customers on it, for example. So do Deutsche Telekom, Cisco, Adobe, and a growing list of governments. ElevenLabs also sells to creators, who use its platform for audiobooks, dubbing, and music. It’s not alone in what it does. In fact, it’s increasingly bumping into customers, including Decagon, a conversational AI platform that trained its voice product on ElevenLabs and now competes with it. But its investors don’t seem too concerned. The company, which says it’s pacing at $600 million in annual recurring revenue, is now reportedly valued at $22 billion by its backers, despite being just four years old. To understand more, I interviewed ElevenLabs co-founder and CEO, Mati Staniszewski, at Nrth in Toronto, a local entrepreneurship conference formerly known as Elevate. We covered a range of topics in a short time, including whether businesses should tell customers when they’re talking to an AI (he thinks they should), and whether he could discuss the company’s gross margins. Unsurprisingly, Staniszewski said he couldn’t discuss them in any detail, but he was clear that he doesn’t mind them getting squeezed even further if it means expanding the company’s market share. Our conversation follows, condensed and lightly edited. You can check out the full conversation here . items.t: Google tests letting Gemini call businesses for you
items.d: Google says the AI-calling feature will first be available to Pixel 11 owners in the U.S. who pay for a Gemini subscription.
items.fullText: With AI agents like Meta’s Muse and Instinct now able to make calls on users’ behalf, Google is now letting Gemini call businesses with a new feature called “Call for Me.” The feature will initially roll out to Pixel 11 owners who pay for a Gemini subscription in the U.S. It will also require the use of the beta version of Google’s Phone app for Android, as it’s still supposed to be an experiment. While Google has long offered calling features guided by AI, prior versions were limited in what they could do. With this update, Gemini will be able to share personal information that you approve as part of the calls it makes, which, the company says, will allow it to take a broader set of actions. In addition, Google says users will be able to follow the call as it happens and take over at any time. “Call for Me” will also use your own personal phone number to make calls, which will be dialed directly from your phone. Google says the AI can handle complex tasks, like calling a store to ask if a product is in stock, making a restaurant reservation, moving a scheduled appointment to a different date, or placing items on hold. The AI can call a business and introduce itself, navigate automated phone menus, wait on hold, and then handle the conversation on the other end. Meanwhile, users can watch how the call proceeds via a live transcript of the conversation. The launch builds on years of experiments with AI-assisted, automated calling technology at Google. Years ago, the company wowed people at its I/O developer conference when it demonstrated Google Assistant calling a salon to make a reservation , and even adding little “umm’s” and “ahh’s” to make the conversation seem natural. items.fullText: 판타지의 경계를 확장하다: 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지가 도쿄게임쇼 2026에서 펼치는 캐릭터 IP와 리테일의 미래 2026/09/23 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 9월 17일부터 20일까지 일본 지바현 마쿠하리 멧세(Makuhari Messe)에서 열린 도쿄게임쇼 2026(Tokyo Game Show 2026, TGS). 글로벌 게임 기업 엔씨 부스는 게임 속 캐릭터를 눈앞에서 만나는 듯한 경험을 하려는 관람객들의 발길이 이어졌다. 그 중심에는 게임의 세계관을 화면 밖으로 확장한 삼성전자의 무안경 3D 디스플레이 ‘스페이셜 사이니지(Spatial Signage)’가 있었다. 이번 행사에서 엔씨가 선보인 ‘아스트라에 오라티오(Astrae Oratio)’는 마법이 일상에 스며든 판타지 세계를 배경으로 한 신전기 서브컬처 RPG다. 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지는 독자적인 ‘3D 플레이트(3D Plate)’ 기술을 적용해 별도의 3D 안경 없이도 콘텐츠에 생생한 입체감을 선사하며, 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 오프라인 전시 공간으로 확장했다. 팬덤 경험 확장… 캐릭터와의 만남을 현실 공간으로 게임 퍼블리셔와 콘텐츠 IP(Intellectual Property, 지식재산권) 보유 기업에게 오프라인 공간은 디지털 콘텐츠를 현실로 가져오는 중요한 접점이다. 엔씨는 도쿄게임쇼에서 85형과 32형 스페이셜 사이니지를 부스 입구와 대기 공간 등에 배치해 관람객이 이동하는 과정에서도 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 자연스럽게 경험하도록 했다. 부스 입구에는 85형 스페이셜 사이니지로 ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 게임의 주요 배경인 ‘특구청’ 건물 내 엘리베이터를 재현했다. 대형 디스플레이를 통해 캐릭터를 실제 사람과 가까운 크기로 표현해, 마치 게임 속 등장인물들이 현실 세계에 인사를 건네는 듯한 장면을 연출했다. ▲ ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 부스 입구에 설치한 85형 스페이셜 사이니지는 게임 속 다양한 캐릭터가 눈 앞으로 다가오는 듯한 연출로 관람객의 이목을 끌었다. 엔씨 아스트라에 오라티오 사업실 이용수 실장은 “관람객들이 부스에 들어서는 순간부터 실제 크기의 캐릭터와 마주하고 게임 세계에 몰입하길 바랐다”면서 “서브컬처 장르에서는 캐릭터의 생동감과 현실감이 특히 중요한데, 스페이셜 사이니지가 이런 특성을 관람객에게 효과적으로 전달할 수 있다고 판단했다”고 말했다. 현장을 찾은 관람객들은 스페이셜 사이니지가 구현한 캐릭터의 크기와 입체감에 주목했다. 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코(Kawaii CoCo) 씨는 “캐릭터가 실제로 움직이며 상호작용하는 것처럼 생생하게 느껴졌다”며 “일반 디스플레이보다 훨씬 눈에 띄고 소셜미디어에서도 근사하게 보일 것 같아, 이 장면을 촬영해 제 구독자들에게 소개하고 싶다”고 말했다. ▲ 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코 씨는 캐릭터의 움직임이 스페이셜 사이니지를 통해 생동감 있게 전달되어 아스트라에 오라티오 부스로 눈길이 갔다고 말했다. 스페이셜 사이니지는 52mm 1 의 얇은 두께에도 불구하고 마치 화면 뒤에 별도의 공간이 있는 듯한 깊이감을 구현한 것이 특징이다. 이러한 경험은 대중에게 게임과 캐릭터의 첫인상을 전달하는 데도 효과적으로 활용될 수 있다. 관람객 다니엘 아세로(Daniel Acero) 씨는 “처음 봤을 때 스크린 화면인 줄 전혀 몰랐고, 투명한 설치물이라고 생각했다”면서 “마치 화면 뒤에 실제 공간이 있는 것처럼 깊이감이 느껴져서 놀라웠고, 이러한 방식으로 게임 캐릭터를 소개하면 게임에 대한 관심을 높이고 캐릭터의 개성을 효과적으로 전달할 수 있을 것”이라고 말했다. 관람객 동선과 대기 공간에는 32형 스페이셜 사이니지가 설치돼 부스 전반으로 캐릭터 경험을 확장했다. 32형 제품은 49.4mm의 얇은 두께로 좁은 공간에도 유연하게 설치가 가능해, 게임 체험을 기다리는 관람객을 대상으로 캐릭터와 세계관에 대한 몰입도를 유지했다. 관람객 토마스 포르티에(Tomas Portier) 씨는 “대기 줄이 길었지만, 스페이셜 사이니지 화면을 items.fullText: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack Open research, controls across the agent stack and continuous testing help defenders build and operate more secure AI systems. September 21, 2026 by Saša Zdjelar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI security is an engineering problem. That means defined security requirements, enforceable controls, named owners and evidence that protections work. As AI becomes more capable, the industry must accelerate security engineering, broaden access to defensive tools and share what works faster. Technology Changes, Security Fundamentals Endure The internet and cloud computing changed how software operates, while core security responsibilities endured: establish identity, control access, limit exposure and verify that protections work. AI agents introduce new capabilities — reasoning, using tools and adapting actions based on the data they encounter. Those capabilities require applying established principles to new operating conditions. This pace creates pressure. Organizations want the productivity benefits of AI while the practices to govern and secure these systems are still developing. Security Depends on the Full Agent Stack Applications depend on code, data, identities, services and infrastructure. Security depends on how those components work together — and AI agents extend that system . Models provide capabilities; harnesses organize context, tools and workflows; and runtime environments provide the infrastructure within which actions execute. Each part of that stack carries security responsibilities, and proper protection requires controls across each layer, as data, instructions and actions move through the system. Consider an agent updating a customer record. Say it encounters malicious instructions in an attached document and attempts to export customer data to an unauthorized destination. items.fullText: University of Manchester Uses NVIDIA Earth-2 to Forecast Air Pollution Across the UK Manchester physicists David Topping and Hao Zhang applied NVIDIA Earth-2 generative models to air quality forecasting — unlocking predictions fast enough to inform public health. September 15, 2026 by Isha Salian 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. alone last year. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run. David Topping, a professor in the University of Manchester’s department of Earth and environmental science, saw that the NVIDIA Earth-2 family of open AI models and tools had cracked a related problem for weather forecasting — and asked whether the same generative frameworks could work for pollution fields. “The biggest challenge is the compute required to forecast air quality,” said Topping. “Once you put chemistry into weather models, they get really, really slow. So I said, why don’t we try using the generative frameworks that NVIDIA develops for climate and weather for pollution fields?” Working with the NVIDIA Earth-2 team, Topping and colleagues generated training data from existing chemistry-climate simulations, then trained Earth-2 CorrDiff — a generative downscaling model — on Isambard-AI, the U.K.’s national AI supercomputer in Bristol. The model worked on the first attempt. items.fullText: ‘Now We Can Know Everything and Do Anything,’ Jensen Huang Says at Dreamforce At Dreamforce, Salesforce and NVIDIA announced Koa, a CRM reasoning model for Agentforce, post-trained from Nemotron on 27 years of Salesforce CRM intelligence — and running entirely within Salesforce’s own infrastructure. September 15, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Know everything. Do anything. That was the message NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang brought to Salesforce Dreamforce Tuesday, joining CEO Marc Benioff onstage in an appearance that coincided with the announcement of Koa — Salesforce’s first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super. Huang didn’t just take the stage. He walked into the crowd — threading through the audience at Moscone Center, mic in hand, with Benioff alongside. “We’re all following you, bro,” Benioff told Huang at one point, drawing applause. “With electricity, we could power everything,” Huang said, tracing the arc of industrial revolutions. “With the internet, you can find anything. And now, with artificial intelligence as an infrastructure layer across the planet, we can know everything and do anything.” That arc led directly to the announcement. Salesforce’s first reasoning model was built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super on a proprietary synthetic dataset drawn from nearly three decades of enterprise CRM deployments. AI Safety When Benioff asked Huang about AI safety, Huang was direct. “Safety is paramount in a lot of ways. It’s job one,” Huang said. “However, safety is an engineering problem.
